text: Dom is a Trans–New Guinea language of the Eastern Group of the Chimbu family, spoken in the Gumine and Sinasina Districts of Chimbu Province and in some other isolated settlements in the western highlands of Papua New Guinea. [2]

title: TransNewGuinea.org
text: TransNewGuinea.org is a database of the Trans-New Guinea language family and friends. The Trans-New Guinea language family currently occupies most of the interior of New Guinea. This family is possibly the third largest in the world with 400 languages and is tentatively thought to have originated with root-crop agriculture around 10,000 years ago.

title: Domu language — Grokipedia
text: The Domu language belongs to the Mailuan family, a subgroup within the extensive Trans-New Guinea phylum of Papuan languages. This classification is supported by comparative linguistic evidence, including shared structural features and vocabulary resemblances that link Mailuan languages to broader Trans-New Guinea patterns.
